v1.name: V1 readiness
v1.summary: The large website-builder repair/rules release is merged and CI-green, but it is not yet proven deployed and a new synthetic run still stopped on an asset-delivery contract bug whose fix remains open.

v2.name: V2 readiness
v2.summary: V2 gained implementation depth through Avery background scheduling, support-knowledge alignment and runtime fixes, but those changes are not fully deployed and the five workers still lack representative real-provider outcome proof.

v3.name: V3 / Full 10/10 vision
v3.summary: The V3 index stays about 60%: website/recovery implementation advanced, but SaaS delivery, automated custom-agent creation, measured economics and proven low-founder-workload operation are largely unchanged.

autonomyProof.note: Individual autonomous proofs exist, but no representative tracked denominator exists yet.

founderWorkload.note: Darius minutes are not consistently separated from customer-required actions, specialist review and operator/contractor work.

dimensions.name: Business understanding & scope selection
dimensions.blocker: Broad real-customer classification and scoping evidence is still limited across varied businesses.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Blind-test 20 varied businesses with no unsupported paid scope accepted.

dimensions.name: Premium website delivery
dimensions.blocker: The merged builder repair/rules release is CI-green but not proven deployed, and synthetic-test25-002 stopped on an asset-delivery contract bug. PR #271 fixes it but remains open.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Merge/review PR #271, deploy the combined builder release, then complete 3 consecutive direction-to-handoff journeys including one injected failure without manual rescue.

dimensions.name: Complete SaaS & existing-app engineering
dimensions.blocker: SelfOperate still has no productized customer workflow that delivers a complete SaaS application with frontend, backend, data, auth, permissions, payments, integrations, tests and deployment.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Deliver one bounded app type end to end through a governed customer workflow, including deployment and handoff.

dimensions.name: Standard AI workforce capability
dimensions.blocker: The five workers have useful implemented slices, but production capability remains uneven; Avery weekly background research is merged but not in the captured production commit, and real provider-backed outcomes for all five remain incomplete.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Deploy Avery background scheduling and record at least one meaningful real-provider outcome for Maya, Jordan, Avery, Alex and Richard.

dimensions.name: Automated custom-agent delivery
dimensions.blocker: The custom-agent slot is still a request/offer path rather than an automated agent-building, independent-testing and activation system.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete one custom agent through supported scope, quote, approval, build, independent tests, practice mode, activation, monitoring and handoff.

dimensions.name: Autonomous coordination & recovery
dimensions.blocker: The merged builder release materially strengthens recovery, but the latest synthetic run still stopped on a recovery-routing contract before any full-study revision. The CI-green fix is unmerged.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Deploy the repaired builder and pass kill/restart/provider/asset-failure tests with preserved progress, correct spend settlement and no manual repair.

dimensions.name: Reliability, security & ongoing maintenance
dimensions.blocker: Production SelfOperate is healthy on the captured revision, but builder release changes are not proven live, the asset-contract failure remains open, and representative restore/soak/incident evidence is incomplete.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete a timed restore drill, a multi-copy soak/failure run and a post-deploy website-builder proof on the same released revision.

dimensions.name: Complete customer journey & ownership
dimensions.blocker: Historical journeys and ownership/export flows exist, but there is still no repeated real paid website cohort through final build, revision, support and handoff. PR #400 shows paused/failed build status still needs an honesty fix.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete 3 paid-like website journeys including revision, a paused/failed recovery case, support, export and final handoff checks.

dimensions.name: Commercial delivery & acquisition readiness
dimensions.blocker: Live checkout and tax are configured, but repeatable acquisition, measured CAC and dependable real-customer conversion remain unproven; production is also nine commits behind main on support/capability-knowledge fixes.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Measure the first source-attributed traffic-to-paid-order funnel and confirm support/capability copy on the deployed revision.

dimensions.name: Economic proof & low-founder-workload operation
dimensions.blocker: There is no representative paid cohort with measured gross margin, failed-attempt cost, retention, support burden, contractor/operator time and Darius intervention time.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Measure the first 5 paid deliveries with provider spend, failed/retried spend, support minutes, contractor/operator minutes and Darius minutes.

v1Remaining: Merge/review CI-green Stromation PR #271 and deploy the combined website-builder release.
Complete at least 3 consecutive directions→build→revision→verification→handoff journeys, including one injected failure/restart, with no hidden manual rescue.
Finish the paused/failed build-status truth contract in Business Builder PR #400 or equivalent and prove it against a stopped build.
v2Remaining: Deploy and prove Avery weekly background research plus meaningful real-provider outcomes for Maya, Jordan, Avery, Alex and Richard.
Expand the actually configured owner integration set and prove recurring SelfOperate operation across several supported business types; catalog entries alone do not count.
Complete dependable monitoring, restore/incident handling and customer ownership/exit proof for the V2 sold scope.
Instrument Darius, operator/contractor, specialist and customer-required minutes so V2 can prove intervention is genuinely falling.
biggestChange: Stromation's 23-commit website-builder repair/rules release (#270) moved from unmerged work to main and all four hosted CI workflows passed. The next realistic synthetic build then exposed an asset-delivery/recovery contract bug: a 26/30 quick draft and $0.42 full concept completed, but the direction stopped because an inline accessible SVG diagram was incorrectly treated as a missing file before any full-study revision ran. PR #271 fixes the contract and all four hosted workflows pass, but it remains open, so the fix receives no implemented-capability credit.
improvements: Stromation PR #270 merged stronger website hard gates, section/library delivery checks, image-feasibility rules, interaction-quality checks and bounded recovery behavior; four hosted CI workflows passed.

Business Builder main is nine commits ahead of the captured production product commit and includes Avery weekly background scheduling/reconciliation, safer shared-SQLite broker reads and support answers aligned with available connections.
The latest production SelfOperate state records healthy web/worker tasks, live Stripe, transactional founder email, Maya's gated sending path and AWS website builder selected.
regressions: The newest synthetic website run exposed an incoherent asset contract and false recovery-stop wording on current Stromation main; the proposed fix is green but unmerged.
Business Builder production is nine commits behind main, so newest support-knowledge, Avery scheduling and runtime fixes are implementation evidence rather than current production behavior.
Build Room can still present paused/failed website progress too optimistically until draft PR #400 receives the final builder reason contract, merges and deploys.

merged: Stromation main f89d202f contains release PR #270, 23 commits ahead of documented deployed builder baseline 5b7cc7f8/rev 38.
Business Builder main 09dca5c9 contains nine commits beyond deployed product 50f9c739.
deployed: Business Builder CURRENT_STATE records production web :268 and worker :138 at product commit 50f9c739 with live Stripe, AWS builder backend and Maya sending enabled subject to owner/safety gates.
No accessible deployment evidence showed Stromation release f89d202f deployed; PR #270 names 5b7cc7f8/rev 38 as its deployed base.
verified: PR #270's four hosted CI workflows passed.
PR #271's four hosted CI workflows pass, but it is still open and gets no implemented-capability credit.
Synthetic-test25-002 proved a 26/30 quick draft and completed full concept study, but also proved the asset-contract failure before handoff.

promisesOverreach: The current website status experience can overstate progress for paused or failed builds until PR #400 or equivalent is deployed.
Any implication that SelfOperate can already build arbitrary complete SaaS products exceeds demonstrated capability.
Any implication that the custom-agent request path is already an automated end-to-end agent factory exceeds demonstrated capability.
Any implication that 95–99% autonomous completion or 1–2 Darius hours/week is already measured exceeds current evidence.
founderWorkloadTrend: Unknown. More work is automated, but intervention time is not instrumented, so evidence cannot yet distinguish true founder-workload reduction from work shifting elsewhere.
nextActions: Review/merge Stromation PR #271, deploy the combined builder release, and rerun synthetic-test25-002 plus the same failure condition.

Run 3 consecutive full website deliveries on the deployed revision, including one controlled failure/restart, and record spend settlement, retries, revisions, final artifact, deployment and handoff without manual rescue.
Finish/deploy honest paused/failed Build Room status, then start recording Darius/operator/customer minutes on every full journey before widening V2 scope.

assumptions: The website-builder asset/recovery defect is fixed and the merged repair release is deployed and repeatedly proven within roughly 30 days.
SelfOperate receives about 150–500 qualified prospects/visitors over 90 days.
Paid conversion is roughly 1–2% while the product remains supervised.
Supervised delivery capacity remains roughly 2–4 projects per month.
Roughly half to three-quarters of eligible delivered customers retain the $299/month ongoing SelfOperate service after any included period.
businessOutlook.note: This is not a reliable demand forecast yet. One-time website/business build revenue is excluded from MRR.

costReporting.measuredSpend: $0.42 for the full concept study in synthetic-test25-002; not the total run or delivery cost.
costReporting.reservedUnconfirmedSpend: Unknown from accessible evidence for the current run.
costReporting.note: Do not combine the $0.42 partial measured spend with older or overlapping estimates.

method: SelfOperate-only assessment for 2026-10-03 using canonical businessbuilder main 09dca5c9, captured production product commit 50f9c739 / web :268 / worker :138, the 2026-10-02 production capability audit, Stromation main f89d202f with merged release PR #270, open CI-green PR #271, Business Builder draft PR #400, hosted workflow results and synthetic-test25-002 evidence. Open PRs receive no implemented-capability credit. Merged code is distinguished from deployed and repeatedly proven behavior.
